Guidance & outlook: If I talk about revenue from operations for Q1 FY27, it stood at INR2,355 million against Q1 FY26 revenue of INR1,930 million, representing a year-on-year growth of 22%.
EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR588 million with an EBITDA margin of 25% against 27% in Q1 FY26.

When I talk about retail business, I am pleased to inform that in continuation with our focus on retail, our retail revenue for the Q1 FY27 stood at INR193 million against revenue of INR118 million in quarter 1 FY'26, growing at impressive year -on-year growth rate of 64% and contributed approximately 9% of overall group revenue.
Growth & demand: Our revenue grew approximately 22% year-on-year in Q1.
More importantly, our like- to-like projects grew approximately 12%.

And just one clarification about the volume growth in fact, while we have seen RPL seeing a kind of robust volume growth, but if we adjust that RPL's volume growth from the reported overall growth, then it looks it is a flat performance for us.
Margins & costs: As regards our margins, as mentioned in the previous quarters, due to the project implementations, they also carry their full fixed cost base from the very first day in laboratory equipment, the manpower and the logistics, while still operating below mature utilization levels, and therefore, you see Krsnaa Diagnostics Limited August 14, 2026 compression in t…

As guided in our previous call, this quarter did carry an element of upfront cost, largely around 4,000 manpower onboarded in Rajasthan logistics across collection center ahead of full revenue realization from the project.
PAT for the quarter stood at INR166 million, translating to a margin of 7%.
Capex & expansion: A related point on capital, ours is an infrastructure-led model and by nature, the capital expenditure is front-ended.

This allows us to serve customers efficiently while keeping our customer acquisition costs structurally lower than those of pure-play Krsnaa Diagnostics Limited August 14, 2026 retail competitors.
Balance sheet & cash: More importantly, this network gives us the scale and infrastructure to progressively drive volumes, improve utilization and unlock the operating leverage embedded in the model.

The infrastructure has been built, the network is scaling and now we are entering the phase where we are expected to invest investments to increasingly translate into the operating leverages and financial performance.
Sir, lastly on the status on receivables of Himachal and Karnataka.
Risks & challenges: So the moderation you see is largely a function of the infrastructure that we have recently built and now are in the process of fulfilling it rather than any pricing or structural pressure in the c ore business.
But simultaneously, I just wanted to check whether the RPL is still -- it is in red at the EBITDA level because there is a kind of a drag or there is a kind of a decline only that we have witnessed.
And along with the recent change in the ministry as well, there has been some delay from a procedure perspective, but we expect money to be collected by Q2.
